points.text: Insufficient discussion and comparison with recent VLM debiasing methods such as B2T
Supervision assumed by each method (spurious, target or validation labels) unclear
Important details deferred to appendix, harder to follow
Only image-encoder attention heads addressed; text-encoder biases ignored
Requires transformer image encoder; not applicable to CLIP-ResNet
Derivation from inequalities to V_S in Eq. 10 unclear
More analysis of spurious association Z_SY in main paper; could it be suppressed too
Locate-and-correct idea not unique; missing related works and benchmark comparisons against them
Direct Effect is not synonymous with an importance score
Theoretical validity of applying causal mediation analysis to neural networks questionable
Paper difficult to read; dense methodology needs diagrams or toy examples
Generalization of located heads across tasks, classes and spurious types underexplored
Protocol needs group/class labels; not truly zero-shot, more supervision than other training-free methods
Label-free LTC-Ŝ results mixed; should be main result with labeled as oracle
Comparison with supervised-label baselines (JTT) unfair, best-configuration reporting
Gender worst-group selection on evaluation set is circular (regression to mean)
Gender evaluation lacks accuracy/utility metric
Anomalous Ortho-Cali ViT-H result uninvestigated
RoboShot gender failure attributed to LLM safeguards without test
LTC equals TextSpan exactly in Table 3; suspicious, no gain
CounterAnimal gains tiny, likely within noise
Ad hoc class pairing and pseudo-label retrieval depart from general framing
Only 45 ImageNet classes evaluated; general performance damage unknown
Linear mixture in Eq. 8 lacks meaning for one-hot votes
Eq. 10 isolation argument heuristic; not validated in controlled setting
Top-1 head votes ignore indirect/MLP effects; direct logit effects not causal; no patching
Threshold γ heuristic with partial sensitivity; λ/γ notation mismatch
Interpretability claims rest on few examples; no quantitative or human evaluation
Explanation of gender S/SY discrepancy speculative
Head-level ablation hides redundancy; concentration of concepts in few heads untested
Only OpenCLIP ViTs; missing CelebA, other spurious benchmarks and CLIP variants
Missing comparisons to recent training-free methods (FairerCLIP, SANER, Kim et al.)
Missing simple head-selection baselines (gradients, activation patching)
No seeds or confidence intervals; small noisy validation set
Headline >50% worst-group gain claim vague and overstated
Minor numeric inconsistencies between tables
Typos and unclear notation
Experimental setup defined late/appendix; key details hard to follow
Several claims asserted without supporting table
